feed.description: Investing conversations for normal humans: frameworks, risk, and the habits that matter more than predictions.
feed.title: Long Horizon Notes

bullets: Index funds are not a strategy but the absence of one — the second-order effect of low-cost structures like Vanguard's is the part most people miss.
Risk management for individual investors is mostly behavioral; the failure mode emerges when market reaction is framed before fundamentals, which most decisions get backwards.
Small value tilts are a point of changed conviction — the tradeoff becomes visible only after internalizing the behavioral framing, otherwise teams rebuild from scratch a year later.
The most underrated piece of index investing is the structural cost advantage pioneered by Vanguard, which enables the second-order effects that matter.
Operational angles for individual investors center on behavioral risk management rather than portfolio mechanics — a pattern that holds across different teams.
Frame is where the conversation gets interesting because the tradeoffs around frame cross-cut everything else covered in the episode.
A practical next step is to pick one idea from the discussion and run it for two weeks — the rest is iteration.
